title: References
summary: Bibliographic references, one folio-reference/v1 node per work: a CSL-JSON item at `references/<key>`, the IRI every `\cite{key}` already points at, read as Dublin Core and BIBO through its JSON-LD.
description: A directory of this kind holds `folio-reference/v1` nodes, one file per reference, named `<key>.json`. A node is a CSL-JSON item (`id` is the citation key) plus `provenance` (authored, catalogue, library or extracted), `derivedFrom` (the asset it was taken from) and `heldAt` (the library asset that holds a copy). It sits at `references/<key>`, where cat-harness `resolveReferenceKey` already sends every cited key, so a citation in the KG resolves instead of dangling. `referenceToJsonLd` reads it as Dublin Core and BIBO; `toCslJson`, `toBibtex`, `toRis` and `toJsonLdGraph` export any set of them. Shape in `folio-assistant-core/schemas/reference.ts`.

avatar.reads: a citation card: one work, its details, its key

rationale: Owner, 2026-10-14 (bean folio-assistant-63q4): a bibliography viewer like the glossary's, with view and export of the bib items in a folio, limited by path to subgraphs and single assets, drawing on library contents, references extracted from papers, Dublin Core records, and references that are not library assets at all. On qou's bibliography the owner ruled '1 + 2': CSL-JSON stays the source, one node per entry. Core's kind by core's rule: a reference describes what a folio holds or cites and where it came from, which is content vocabulary, not harness. `content`: references are authored or derived by an import process, and a detached reference still says something standing on its own. Distinct from `catalogue` (a remote corpus by reference) and `library` (bytes held here): a reference describes a WORK, whether or not any copy is held, and points at the library asset with `heldAt` when one is.
